name: Time-delay push switch plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a push switch that turns lights on for a set period, commonly used in stairwells and common corridors.
description: A time-delay push switch, often wired to a staircase timer, turns lighting on when pressed and lets it switch off after a set interval. Plans draw a push-button mark at each push position with a small clock or t tag, and show the timer location in the board where one is used.

Several push switches may be wired in parallel to one timer, so the switching line links them all to a common luminaire group. The electrician reads the plan to run a separate push conductor rather than switched-line wiring.
The plan symbol does not set the delay period or state whether the timer is in the switch or at the board. The specification should give both.
readingNotes: Look for the associated timer in the board schedule.
Expect several pushes wired in parallel on one landing group.
drawingChecklist: State delay time and adjustment range.
Link all pushes to the controlled group.
distinction: A momentary bell push is not connected to lighting; a time-delay push switch starts a lighting timer.
